rationale: Start with a broad mid-strength scouting gradient at moderate temperature to map the elution window for all 10 compounds while reducing risk of truncation. This should reveal whether the mixture is generally early or late eluting and where the critical pairs lie.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the objective is now to reduce t_last below 10 min by steepening the gradient while holding selectivity constant. A moderate step from 20 to 16 min should cut run time with limited risk of dropping the current worst pair below 1.5.

The current method is close to the 10 min target and the limiting pair still has some margin, so a further small decrease in tG is the most direct way to try to eliminate the remaining time penalty. This tests whether we can push t_last under 10 min before resolution of the 6/7 pair falls below 1.5.

We are now in the regime where selectivity, not time, is limiting: t_last is already under 10 min, but the 6/7 pair has slipped below 1.5. Lowering temperature one step may recover enough selectivity for that critical pair while likely keeping the last peak near or under 10 min.

The 14 min method is already fast enough, so we should restore full resolution by slightly relaxing the gradient while probing whether a modest temperature increase can keep the last peak at or below 10 min. This targets the narrow optimum between 16 min/40 C (resolved but too slow) and 14 min/40 C (fast but slightly under-resolved).

Keep the successful 16 min, 40 C selectivity conditions but lower phi1 one step to strengthen retention of the latest compounds and potentially pull the critical mid-cluster apart. This checks whether a narrower gradient window can improve the limiting pair enough to reach full resolution without pushing t_last too far above 10 min.

The main issue is the crowded mid-eluting cluster, while the early peaks have far more spacing than needed. Raising phi0 one step should compress the early region and redistribute gradient strength later, potentially improving the critical 6/7 separation while preserving the already acceptable t_last under 10 min.

Changing phi0 upward did not fix the limiting pair, so test the opposite direction to see whether a lower starting strength improves selectivity in the crowded 5–7 region while keeping the run under 10 min. This is a targeted selectivity probe around the current near-optimal 14 min, 40 C condition.

At 16 min, lowering phi1 improved the critical pair substantially but cost too much time; at 14 min we may keep t_last under 10 min while gaining enough resolution on 6/7. This directly tests whether reducing the gradient end strength can convert the near-miss 14 min method into a fully resolved, penalty-free run.

We have achieved the maximum CRF, so the only remaining goal is to see whether an even shorter method can preserve full resolution and stay at the score ceiling. Shortening tG by one step around the successful phi1 0.85 condition is the most efficient way to test for a faster equally optimal method.

Since 12 min lost too much resolution, keep the successful 14 min/0.85 window and test whether a 5 C higher temperature can pull t_last more comfortably below 10 min while retaining enough separation of the critical 6/7 pair. This explores whether there is another score-1.000 condition with a slightly shorter actual run time margin.

The optimum is clearly sensitive around the 6/7 pair, so test a further one-step reduction in phi1 at the successful 14 min, 40 C conditions to see whether added selectivity is offset by only a small time increase. This probes whether another fully resolved method exists on the shorter/stronger edge of the optimum basin.

The successful method likely sits on a narrow balance between phi0 and phi1, so pairing the stronger-start condition with the improved end point is the next logical selectivity test. This checks whether compressing the early region while keeping the gentler final elution can preserve full resolution and move t_last a bit earlier.

This is now the fastest fully resolved family found, so the next step is to see whether it can be shortened one increment while retaining the 6/7 pair above 1.5. If successful, it would match the maximum CRF with a shorter actual run than the current best methods.

Since the 0.15/0.85/14 method is fully resolved with some margin on the critical pair, a one-step increase in phi0 may further shorten the late retention while staying on the same favorable selectivity surface. This tests whether the score-1.000 region extends to a faster practical method.

The 0.15/0.85/14 method is optimal, and lowering phi1 at phi0 0.10 increased the critical-pair resolution but made the run slightly too late. Testing the same phi1 reduction with phi0 0.15 may keep the stronger 6/7 separation while preserving t_last under 10 min.

We already have score-1.000 methods, so the remaining opportunity is to map nearby conditions that might also be robustly optimal. A one-step temperature increase from the current best 0.15/0.85/14 method tests whether faster elution can be gained without losing the critical 6/7 resolution margin.

With the maximum CRF already reached, use remaining injections to map robustness around the optimum. Extending tG one step at phi0 0.15, phi1 0.90 should reveal whether a broader fully resolved plateau exists in this part of method space and how much safety margin the critical 6/7 pair can gain.

We have bracketed the optimum with phi0 and phi1 separately, but not yet tested their combined effect. This combination may keep the late peak within 10 min while restoring more resolution to the critical 6/7 pair, helping define the true boundary of the score-1.000 region.

This is another score-1.000 family, so the key remaining test is whether it can be shortened one gradient step without losing the critical 6/7 separation. A successful result would identify the shortest fully resolved method found so far.

The score-1.000 region appears to continue toward higher phi0 while the 6/7 pair is the only hard boundary. A one-step increase in phi0 from the successful 0.20/0.80/14 method tests whether an even faster practical method remains fully resolved or whether the optimum edge has been reached.

Higher phi0 has now reached the early-elution failure boundary, so the remaining unexplored direction is lower phi1 from the successful 0.20/0.80/14 optimum. This tests whether added end-of-gradient retention can preserve full resolution and still keep the last peak under 10 min.

With three injections left and multiple score-1.000 methods already found, it is useful to map a cooler, slightly shallower condition as a robustness check away from the known temperature-sensitive failure at 45 C. This should show whether lower temperature can maintain full resolution in a broader operating window, even if it is unlikely to beat the best score.

One useful boundary remains untested: whether the stronger-retaining 0.20/0.75 condition can be shortened to 12 min and still keep the critical 6/7 pair resolved. This directly probes for a shorter penalty-free method adjacent to the score-1.000 region.

The last remaining informative edge test is whether lowering phi1 rescues the early-pair collapse seen at phi0 0.25, while still maintaining the critical 6/7 separation. This maps the high-phi0 boundary of the score-1.000 region and confirms whether the optimum truly tops out at phi0 0.20.
